ear_left: All the News of the Frontier
motto: Land, Labor & Lead — No Path is Predetermined
population: %s of %s souls in the Territory today
story_1_deck: Land, Labor and Lead Await the Bold
story_1_body: From the cattle country to the Lemoyne bayou, the Territories stand open to any soul with grit enough to claim a living. No path is laid out in advance. A man may swing a pick, wear a badge or ride with a gang, and a woman may run a saloon or rob the very bank that holds her deed. Every choice carries weight, and the Territories remember.
story_2_headline: Dirty Money Sits Heavy in the Pocket
story_2_deck: No Deed, No Business Bought With Blood
story_2_body: The land office and the bank are of one mind: money taken at gunpoint will not buy a deed, a business or a civic charter. Outlaws who wish to spend like honest folk must first see their blood money washed through a front, and the launderer keeps his cut. Crime pays, the saying goes, but it pays in a currency of its own.
story_3_headline: Word Travels Fast in the Territories
story_3_deck: Shopkeepers Mind Who Walks Through Their Door
story_3_body: An honest name is worth money on Main Street: decent folk find the storekeeper's prices kinder. A fearsome name opens other doors, in back rooms where the law does not drink. Rumors move between towns quicker than the mail coach, so mind what you do and who sees you do it.
story_4_headline: A Fair Day's Wage on the Frontier
story_4_body: A hot meal at the saloon runs a nickel or a dime. A bed for the night costs a quarter to a dollar. A sound working horse fetches fifteen to thirty-five dollars, and a fine-blooded mount far more. Spend wisely, settler: every coin in these parts was earned by somebody's labor, risk or cunning.
story_5_headline: Saloons and Shops For Sale to Honest Buyers
story_5_deck: Owners May Hire Hands and Keep the Books
story_5_body: Enterprising citizens may purchase a saloon or general store with clean money, set their own prices, hire hands and keep the takings in a secure business account. The land office takes no blood money for a business, though what an owner does in the back room is between him and his conscience.
path_1_text: Hunt, trap, mine, farm and haul. Work up from day labor to cattle drives, freight lines and a business of your own.
path_2_text: Hold up the roads, rob the trains and crack the banks. Quick money, paid in blood, with a bounty never far behind.
path_3_text: Honest by day, crooked by night. Run a front, wash dirty money for a cut and pull the strings from the shadows.
wanted_text: Of good character or otherwise. Must be able to ride, shoot or swing a pick.
notice_1: Carry a fortune and you carry a target. Bank what you can.
notice_2: Every gunfight needs a reason. Random violence is not welcome in the Territories.
notice_3: Read the rules before you ride. Ignorance is no defense before the judge.
notice_4: Blood money may be washed clean through a front, but the launderer always keeps a cut.
notice_5: You may change your road at any time. No settler is bound to one path forever.
